Issues at the Cyberville’s Water Treatment Plant...

Hey guys!! I'm a Black Hat, like the bad guy in a story. I used to use my computer skills to do bad things, like break into systems, steal information, cause trouble, and spread viruses. But recently, a close friend dared me to help him againts another Black Hat who had spread a MALWARE in the Water Treatment Plant in his Cyberville. That made me realize that doing such things can hurt millions of people, even those you care about. So I decided that I don't want to be a Black Hat anymore, but to do that, first I need to create an antivirus against this malware. If you want to help me, I have this information that will be useful.

What does the virus do?

First, you need to download this b.Board code to start https://www.brilliantlabs.ca/documents/cybersec/M2-Water-Plant-Black-Hat.hex Second, go to code-alpha.brilliantlans.ca and drag and drop this file into a new project to code. As you will see, the Chloride and Fluoride level bars don't work properly because of the virus.

You can also download the base code to examine the system's proper functioning. In the original setup, the Chloride and Fluoride levels behave as expected according to the code. For instance, when you set a [Chloride level: 3], the output will display a level of 3. Similarly, when you set a [Fluoride level: 3], the output will also reflect a level of 3. This demonstrates 👍 Proper functioning.

However, once the VIRUS is introduced by the Black Hat, the proportion between Chloride (CL) and Fluoride (FL) becomes faulty. For example, when you set a [Chloride level: 3], the system might output a level of 17, and for a [Fluoride level: 3], it could display a level of 21. This highlights the 👎 Improper functioning caused by the virus.


Currently, the microbit is already providing some useful feedback. I have observed that the microbit screen at coordinates (0,4) corresponds to a value of 10, which scales to represent the Chloride level selection. Similarly, coordinates (0,3) correspond to a value of 20, while coordinates (0,2) indicate a value of 30, and so on. Additionally, there is a distinct line in the middle of the microbit display. A brighter section of this line suggests that the screen is divided, with Chloride levels shown on the left side and Fluoride levels on the right.


I just wanted to share some info I found from a previous test I did. It's about how to read the levels affected by the malware. I hope it helps!


How can I counteract the virus?

Unfortunately, I'm not sure exactly how to do that. However, I know that Black Hats love math, they enjoy adding, subtracting, multiplying, and dividing numbers—so that might be a clue. In my experience as a Black Hat, I've learned that to deal with a virus, you need to break it down. We will need one antivirus for Chloride and another for Fluoride. Fortunately, in Mission 2, we have cybersecurity blocks that can serve as our antivirus. It is crucial to complete the Attack-Tree Analysis to document what the viruses are doing, and to solve this challenge.


Attack-Tree Analysis

You can get a copy of the Attack-tree Analysis page from your teacher. Once you have it, you can use the terminal at https://cyberville.brilliantlabs.ca/terminal.html to introduce the commands that will give you the right antivirus number values. I hope this helps!


What is the expected result?

Everything should be fine if Dr. Olivia from the Water Treatment Plant Aqua Pure Technologies selects the correct levels of Chloride and Fluoride, and these levels are properly represented on the bars, and the microbit screen totally clear.
